                    ### Question
                    A 21-year-old man went to the emergency room after presenting several episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures in the last week. In the cranial CT scan, a unilocular cystic lesion was observed with a small nodule attached to the wall corresponding to the encysting larva of a parasite. Which of the following pathogens can be responsible ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Entamoeba histolytica.
opb. Cryptococcus neoformans.
opc. Taenia saginata
opd. Taenia solium

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Taenia solium and Taenia saginata can both cause larval forms to encyst in different tissues, with Taenia solium leading to neurocysticercosis when encysted in the brain. The presence of a cystic lesion with a small nodule in the brain suggests Taenia solium as the likely pathogen responsible for the patient's symptoms.
